Just a modicum of dignity is all it takes
To break bread with the Spirit of The Greats.
But dignity is mercurial, a fugitive stag,
Behind which our better judgements lag.
They remain present, though, heaven sent and
Better for this ought be the judge - yet,
Left to fester without courage bent,
Or purpose set,
Upon the greater portion found in the lesser,
Nothing better is met,
Though the gavel in hand,
Til dignity’s quiet power grows in the chamber - pressure.
